main_text.head: PRÆLECTIO QUARTA,
In quâ Quæ sit Adæquata Conscientiæ Regula disquiritur & statuitur.
JAC. 4. 12.

p.i: Unus enim est Legislator, qui potest servare & perdere.

main_text.p: QUàm parùm sit unicuique præsidii, ad Conscientiæ suæ sive fructum, ad excusandum ea quæ hactenus fecerit, sive securitatem ad ἀφόβως aggrediendum quæ porrò facturus est, si ea aut sola boni finis intentione, aut aliena tantùm exempli vel judicii authoritate nituntur: satis à me superque proximis duabus prælectionibus demonstratum est. Eo nimirum consilio, ut sublatis è medio his velut obicibus, expeditior mihi & complanatior esset via, ad ea quæ de Conscientiæ obligatione dicere instituera m. Quæ Obligatio cùm sit duplex: Activa scilicet, per quam alterius obligationi sub-est: postulat ordinis ratio, ut à passiva ordiamur. Tunc enim de re mensurata securius pronunciare poterimus,

page.notes: The left page is only a sliver at the scan edge; its lines are cut off and are given as one fragment. Show-through: faint mirrored text across the upper part of the right page (under the title area and the top margin) is not printed on this page and is left out; no running head is legible as printed text. The "J" in "Jecuritatem" is printed as a long s and is transcribed as securitatem. The Greek word ἀφόβως and the "m" in "instituera m." are as far as I can read them; the line in the upper part of the text is clear but the Greek accents may be imperfect. The left-margin "Æ." sits at the cut edge and is not included.
